subject: ela
intro: This test covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for informational text across all three standards: using details and inferences (4.RI.A.1), main idea and summary (4.RI.A.2), and explaining events, procedures, and ideas including why they happen (4.RI.A.3). Each question is multiple choice and labeled with the standard it checks.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A cactus can live in the dry desert because it stores water. When rain finally falls, the cactus soaks up as much water as it can and holds it inside its thick stem. This stored water keeps the cactus alive during the long dry months.

Where does a cactus store its water?
A) In its roots
B) In its thick stem
C) In its flowers
D) In the sand

steps: The question asks where water is stored.
The text says the cactus "holds it inside its thick stem."
So the answer is B.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Wolves live and hunt in a family group called a pack. By working together, a pack can bring down animals much larger than a single wolf could. The pack shares the food it catches.

What is a group of wolves called?
A) A herd
B) A flock
C) A pack
D) A school

steps: The question asks for a stated word.
The text says wolves live in "a family group called a pack."
So the answer is C.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A skunk does not want to fight. When an animal comes too close, the skunk first stamps its feet and raises its tail as a warning. If the animal still does not leave, only then does the skunk spray its terrible smell.

What can you infer about why the skunk stamps its feet first?
A) It is trying to dance
B) It is warning the animal to leave before it sprays
C) It is looking for food
D) It is trying to dig a hole
items.answer: B) It is warning the animal to leave before it sprays

steps: The reason is hinted, so I infer it.
The text calls the stamping and raised tail "a warning" and says it sprays only if the animal "still does not leave."
So the stamping is a warning first, answer B.
solution.answer: B) It is warning the animal to leave before it sprays

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Inside a busy beehive, a bee that finds flowers does a special "waggle dance" when it returns. The dance points in the direction of the flowers, and the length of the dance tells how far away they are. Other bees watch closely, then fly straight out to the same flowers.

What can you infer is the purpose of the waggle dance?
A) To make the hive warmer
B) To tell other bees where to find flowers
C) To clean the hive
D) To scare away the queen
items.answer: B) To tell other bees where to find flowers

steps: I combine clues to infer the purpose.
The dance shows the "direction" and "how far" the flowers are, and other bees then "fly straight out to the same flowers."
So the dance tells bees where the flowers are, answer B.
solution.answer: B) To tell other bees where to find flowers

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A balanced meal keeps your body strong. Fruits and vegetables give you vitamins. Bread and rice give you energy to run and play. Milk and beans help build strong bones and muscles.

What is the main idea of this passage?
A) Milk tastes good
B) A balanced meal keeps your body strong
C) Rice is white
D) Vegetables are green
items.answer: B) A balanced meal keeps your body strong

steps: The first sentence states the big point.
The rest give ways different foods help the body.
So the main idea is B.
solution.answer: B) A balanced meal keeps your body strong

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The old bridge in town was closed for repairs, so the city set up a free ferry boat across the river. People still got to work on time. Shops on the far side stayed busy. Once the bridge reopened, everyone agreed the ferry had saved the day.

Which detail best supports the main idea that the ferry helped the town?
A) The bridge was old
B) People still got to work on time
C) The river was wide
D) The bridge reopened
items.answer: B) People still got to work on time

steps: The main idea is that the ferry helped the town.
I look for a detail showing a benefit.
"People still got to work on time" shows how the ferry helped, so B.
solution.answer: B) People still got to work on time

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Sea turtles face many dangers from the moment they hatch. Baby turtles must race across the open sand to the sea while birds try to grab them. In the water, big fish hunt them. Out of a hundred hatchlings, only a few will live to grow up.

Which is the best summary of this passage?
A) Baby sea turtles hatch from eggs.
B) Sea turtles face many dangers from birds and fish, so only a few hatchlings survive to grow up.
C) Birds live near the beach.
D) The ocean is very big.
items.answer: B) Sea turtles face many dangers from birds and fish, so only a few hatchlings survive to grow up.

steps: A good summary gives the main idea and key details.
Choices A, C, and D are only small details.
Choice B captures the dangers and the low survival, so B.
solution.answer: B) Sea turtles face many dangers from birds and fish, so only a few hatchlings survive to grow up.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

When a new highway cut through the forest, animals could no longer safely cross to reach food and mates. So the town built a bridge covered with grass and trees just for wildlife. Deer, bears, and even turtles began using it. Fewer animals were hurt on the road, and the separated parts of the forest were joined again.

Which sentence best states the main idea of this passage?
A) Highways are made of concrete
B) A wildlife bridge let animals cross safely and reconnected the forest
C) Turtles move slowly
D) The forest had many trees
items.answer: B) A wildlife bridge let animals cross safely and reconnected the forest

steps: I ask what the passage is mostly about.
It explains how the wildlife bridge solved the problem of animals being cut off.
Choices A, C, and D are small details, so the main idea is B.
solution.answer: B) A wildlife bridge let animals cross safely and reconnected the forest

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

To make orange juice, first wash the oranges. Next, cut each orange in half. Then press each half against a juicer to squeeze out the juice. Finally, pour the juice into a glass.

According to the text, what do you do right after you cut the oranges in half?
A) Wash the oranges
B) Press each half against a juicer
C) Pour the juice into a glass
D) Peel the oranges
items.answer: B) Press each half against a juicer

steps: I find the step after cutting the oranges.
The text says, "Then press each half against a juicer."
So the answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Press each half against a juicer

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Rust forms on metal over time. When iron metal is left out in wet air, the water and air slowly attack the surface. Bit by bit, a flaky orange coating called rust builds up. This is why tools left out in the rain turn orange and crumbly.

According to the text, why does rust form on metal?
A) The metal gets too cold
B) Wet air slowly attacks the iron surface
C) The Sun paints it orange
D) People rub it with sand
items.answer: B) Wet air slowly attacks the iron surface

steps: I look for the cause of rust.
The text says "the water and air slowly attack the surface," building up rust.
So the answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Wet air slowly attacks the iron surface

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

In the 1930s, many families lost their jobs and money during a hard time called the Great Depression. To help, the government created programs that paid people to build roads, bridges, and parks. This gave workers a paycheck and left the country with things everyone could use.

According to the text, why did the government pay people to build roads and bridges?
A) To make the roads look pretty
B) To give jobless people work and a paycheck during a hard time
C) To sell the roads to other countries
D) To keep people out of the parks
items.answer: B) To give jobless people work and a paycheck during a hard time

steps: I find the reason for the building programs.
The text says the programs were created "to help" people who "lost their jobs" and gave workers "a paycheck."
So the answer is B.
solution.answer: B) To give jobless people work and a paycheck during a hard time

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Why do our ears sometimes pop on a tall mountain or in an airplane? The air presses on your eardrum from both the outside and the inside. When you rise up high quickly, the air pressure outside drops, but the pressure inside your ear stays the same for a moment. That difference pushes on the eardrum until a tiny tube opens and lets the air even out with a pop.

According to the text, why do ears pop when you go up high quickly?
A) The mountain is loud
B) Cold air freezes the ear
C) The air pressure outside drops while the pressure inside stays the same for a moment
D) Water gets trapped in the ear
items.answer: C) The air pressure outside drops while the pressure inside stays the same for a moment

steps: I trace the cause of the pop.
Going up fast makes the outside pressure drop while inside pressure "stays the same for a moment."
That difference pushes the eardrum until air evens out, so C.
solution.answer: C) The air pressure outside drops while the pressure inside stays the same for a moment
